title: Fundamental-derivative criticality of ion-acoustic solitons in fluid-Poisson plasmas with general equations of state
html:
Abstract:Non-ideal ion compressibility modifies the nonlinearity of ion-acoustic waves. In a fluid-Poisson plasma with Boltzmann electrons and a barotropic ion equation of state, we relate the quadratic KdV coefficient to the fundamental derivative of the effective acoustic pressure. Its vanishing marks loss of genuine nonlinearity. Higher derivatives of the equation of state determine whether the cubic reduction is focusing or defocusing and govern the quartic-flux reduction at simultaneous criticality. The exact Sagdeev formulation resolves compressive and rarefactive soliton branches and their Gardner unfolding. Exact continuation identifies an equation-of-state-controlled rarefactive double-layer boundary distinct from both the cubic critical point and an orbitwise pressure-slope threshold. As they approach this boundary, solitons develop a logarithmically widening flat top, and the exact Sagdeev quadrature quantitatively captures the standard saddle-passage law. Along the boundary toward the acoustic codimension-two point, exponential localisation lengths diverge while the amplitude vanishes. Full fluid-Poisson simulations confirm finite-time propagation of selected exact stationary profiles. Our results connect acoustic criticality, exact orbit admissibility, and equation-of-state-controlled solitary waves in dispersive plasmas.
